decisions.reason: The air quality sensor extends existing analog/digital sensor and firmware knowledge, so the firm can assimilate early results and improve it.
As a direct replacement of the Analog In Bricklet 2.0, it builds on proven in-house analog input and firmware capabilities.
The MQTT proxy leverages the firm's existing software bindings, API generation, and connectivity know-how.
CAN bus is a communication protocol within the firm's connectivity expertise, though it requires protocol stack work, which the firm can learn.
CO2 sensing uses sensor integration and calibration knowledge similar to air quality, allowing the firm to interpret results and cooperate with sensor suppliers.
The touch panel accessory builds on modular hardware, 3D models, and documentation, but requires UI/display capabilities that are less central, so some uncertainty remains.
